findings.finding: The plan states that `cli-compat.probe-spawn.test.ts` (the sync suite) will be "unchanged and still green" (Step 2 and 3). However, the plan also states that splitting the module removes the need for `versionProbeSpawn` to use a `try/catch` since it can just check for `null`. If `cli-compat.ts` drops the `try/catch` block and checks for `null`, the test file will almost certainly require modifications to update its mock (returning `null` instead of throwing) or to adjust assertions covering the "executable not found" path.

AC-9 is internally incompatible with the planned deletion of `cli-compat.probe-spawn-async.test.ts`. It requires that “no collected test disappeared” and “no coverage [be] removed,” while the plan explicitly deletes 11 collected tests and acknowledges deliberate coverage reduction. A behavior-snapshot verifier cannot truthfully satisfy both conditions.
findings.suggestion: Adjust the simplify verification ledger/AC-9 to explicitly allow the 11 deleted tests and their associated coverage only when attributable to deletion of `probeClaudeVersionAsync`. Keep the requirement that no unrelated test disappears, flips from green to red, or loses coverage, and reconcile before/after counts accordingly.

findings.finding: The plan identifies `path.win32.extname` and the `SystemRoot` fallback `join` as pure-string decisions, but it does not explicitly require an audit of every other path-derived string decision in both implementations. In particular, resolver code commonly also uses `isAbsolute`, `basename`, `normalize`, `parse`, `relative`, and `delimiter`; any of these used to classify a Windows command or parse `PATH`/`PATHEXT` can retain host-POSIX behavior under a stubbed Win32 platform.
findings.suggestion: Before implementation, enumerate every `path.` use in both resolver copies and classify it as either (a) Win32 command-string semantics (`path.win32`) or (b) host-filesystem access (host `path`). Add pins for any classification-sensitive behavior, especially extension detection and any `PATH` splitting/classification. Preserve host `resolve`/`join` only at the point that turns an already-selected candidate into a path to stat/access on the actual host filesystem.

findings.finding: The host-filesystem exception in AC-6 can become ambiguous when test inputs contain multiple `PATH` entries or Windows-style separators. A POSIX-host test that stubs Win32 needs host-addressable directories, while a production Windows resolver normally interprets Windows `PATH` formatting. Merely changing some APIs to `path.win32` can cause tests to pass for a single planted directory but mishandle multi-entry or separator-sensitive cases.
findings.suggestion: Define and test the boundary explicitly: use Windows semantics for command-token parsing and extension classification, but inject or isolate the host-search-path representation used by the fs-touching lookup in tests. At minimum, add a test with more than one search-path entry plus a planted executable in a later entry, so the chosen delimiter behavior is intentional rather than incidental.

findings.finding: AC-10 is described as exercising “real Windows `.cmd`/`.exe` resolution,” but the proposed runner description does not explicitly require a Windows worker or a controlled supported Claude CLI fixture. On a non-Windows runner it cannot exercise the production path semantics, and against a developer/CI-installed Claude it is environment-dependent (missing CLI, unsupported version, or an unrelated user configuration can fail the check).
findings.suggestion: Make a Windows execution environment and a deterministic CLI fixture/prerequisite explicit for AC-10. The fixture should provide a supported version and the relevant executable form (`.cmd` and/or `.exe`) on the search path, with diagnostics configured to use it. If the existing F0.5 infrastructure cannot provide that, retain the web check as a boot-regression test but do not claim it verifies real Windows command resolution.

findings.finding: The direct source-scan proposed for the new core module is useful but insufficient by itself to establish that `cli-compat` no longer reaches the preview-session-manager ESM cycle. It can prove no direct import exists while an indirect import through a new or existing dependency still restores the cycle. This matters because the cycle removal is a stated reason for the extraction and the module is security-load-bearing.
findings.suggestion: Keep the direct “no preview import” source assertion, but also add or retain a boot/module-load regression check that imports the actual `cli-compat` boot path in the relevant configuration and verifies it initializes without loading the preview dependency chain. AC-10 may serve this purpose only if it is deterministic and runs in the intended environment.

findings.finding: The new null-returning core contract is well chosen, but the approach should preserve more than the preview success/failure result. Extraction can subtly alter command/argument handling for empty argv, quoted executable paths, explicit extensions with mixed casing, and absolute/relative Windows-looking command paths. The frozen preview guard protects selected security cases but may not cover all core call patterns used by `cli-compat`.
findings.suggestion: Build the new core test suite from the existing resolver cases before moving code, and add explicit contract tests for empty/invalid argv, quoted paths, explicit `.cmd`/`.exe` extensions, and unresolved bare names. Verify that only the intentional unresolvable-bare-name return conversion differs between core and preview wrapper; all other errors and resolved `{ command, args, windowsVerbatimArguments }` values should remain identical.  Overall, the extraction and thin throwing wrapper are the sound, minimal design for breaking the boot-time preview dependency while preserving preview behavior. Resolve the contradictory verification criterion, fully audit path-semantics calls, and make the Windows end-to-end prerequisite deterministic before implementation. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
